subject: Oceanography
title: Fishing Down the Food Web
description: A quick, practical guide to Fishing Down the Food Web.

hook.text: We used to catch big predatory fish—now we're fishing smaller species lower on the food chain.

buildup.text: Daniel Pauly coined 'fishing down the food web'—describing how we deplete top predators then target their prey.

discovery.text: The mean trophic level of global catches has declined steadily since the 1950s—we're eating lower on the chain.

twist.text: Catching forage fish (anchovies, sardines) for fish meal starves the predators that remain—a vicious cycle.

climax.text: If trends continue, jellyfish may dominate future oceans—thriving where fish have been removed.

punchline.text: We ate the big fish, then the medium fish—now we're eating what's left.

quiz.question: What does 'fishing down the food web' mean?
options: Depleting top predators then targeting smaller species
